summary: Each round you blind-bid coins across four taverns to determine turn order, then draft dwarves in descending bid order while your coin values grow via a satisfying 'coin-building' upgrade mechanic. It plays fast and tense, with a light push-your-luck feel around guessing what others will bid and when to hire the big-value heroes.
praised: Clever coin-upgrading mechanism that ties bidding directly into economy growth
Fast, tense rounds with meaningful blind-bid tension
Easy to teach, quick to play, scales well 2-5
Great production/art and satisfying tactile coin play
High replayability from varied dwarf/hero combos
criticised: Can feel a bit solitaire/multiplayer-solitaire since interaction is indirect
Randomness in which heroes/dwarves appear can swing scoring
Some find the five scoring categories fiddly to track and optimize
Endgame scoring math can be a bit dry/calculation-heavy

interaction.kind: simultaneous blind bidding that indirectly blocks others from cards/turn order

scoring.why: final score sums five different dwarf-type categories plus heroes and gold, so balancing multiple scoring tracks decides the winner
